goal: Hook: the class watches a Germaine Acogny solo, described and linked, notices how its moves start from a wave of the spine, and meets the compelling question; the warm-up and the stop cue are reopened and the spots marked.
note: Work: Acogny solo picked by the unit plan (Senegal, Ecole des Sables); the sensitivity agent reads the school pages first; students make their own aligned shapes and do not copy her technique as a style. Responding and connecting touched (where, who, for what). Equipment: floor tape or chalk spots, a hand drum or a pot and wooden spoon. Hazards and controls: floor cleared and checked for spills and objects before the session; bare feet or soft-soled shoes, never socks on a smooth floor; an arm length between dancers when traveling; level changes slow, knees and hands first; no lifts and no weight-sharing; partner contact only by agreement and never required; the stop cue used; water and rest offered. Weekly path: session 1.

goal: The alignment check (feet, knees, hips, head stacked) shown in named steps with the alignment card, then a short sequence of shapes, qualities and patterns copied with the body aligned and strong.
note: Retrieval task (10 minutes after the warm-up): grade 2 pathways and adjusting, and direction, phrases and strong beats, danced and named. By course order: one ten-minute reteach of both grade 2 steps together, inside the same block, for a student or class that did not take the grade 2 year. set-up 3, warm-up 5, retrieval 10, teaching 15, cool-down 4, room back 3. Weekly path: session 1.

goal: The copied sequence danced three times with the alignment check between tries and one teacher comment each time.
note: Baseline look at the unit main look-for, rotating groups, marked met, partly or not yet; not scored, it is the first of two marks for growth. A student who cannot move freely dances a seated or one-limb version, mapped to the same look-for. Weekly path: session 2.

goal: Space shown in steps with the elements card: distance between dancers judged, all three dimensions, filled and empty space, eyes leading the move; the class watches a Pilobolus piece shaping the empty space between dancers.
note: Work: a Pilobolus piece the unit plan picks, described and linked. Its lifts are watched only; the class makes every shape on each student own spot. Responding touched. Weekly path: session 2.

goal: The partner signal (look, nod, go) shown, then level, direction and path changes made safely with a partner and in a small group.
note: Level changes to the floor slow, knees and hands first, no dropping; partner contact only by agreement, never required. Weekly path: session 2.

goal: Partner level, direction and path changes run in short rounds with the signal, beside a dimension drill (up and down, side to side, forward and back).
note: Shorter year: fold-in day (see the scope and sequence). Weekly path: session 3.

goal: Set counts of 8 and 16 shown on the drum; the class improvises to fill the count and end on its last beat, first with the accompaniment and then against it, in metric phrases and in phrases led by breath and flow.
note: Counts are said and clapped; no number is written (math contact only). Creating touched by the improvisation. Drum at a moderate volume. Weekly path: session 3.

goal: Energy and dynamics shown in pairs of opposites (strong and light, sharp and smooth); one move danced four ways to give it a clear quality for an intent.
note: Words: energy, dynamics. Weekly path: session 4.

goal: Improvisation drill: fill a count of 16 using two energy qualities, three rounds with a partner watching for the last beat.
note: Shorter year: fold-in day (see the scope and sequence). Weekly path: session 4.

goal: The recall card shown: dance it, check it, take one coach comment, dance it again; pairs recall the copied sequence and use the self-check to improve it.
note: The phrase-recall model starts here. Weekly path: session 4.

goal: Groups of five build their showing with some choice: the copied sequence, a partner change, and an improvised section that fills a set count with two qualities.
note: Creating touched (the group choices). Arm length kept while traveling. Weekly path: session 5.

goal: Critique day: each group dances for a partner group, takes describe, ask and suggest comments, and chooses one change.
note: The unit one critique (describe, ask, suggest), each comment tied to a look-for, praise alone is not feedback; the teacher marks the record sheet; each group chooses one change and says it in one line. First use of the feedback-loop routine, modeled here and owned in unit 4. Responding touched. Weekly path: session 5.

goal: The change rehearsed; each group recalls its sequence with no teacher cue, and the recall card records the comment, the self-check and the improvement.
note: The step cards are withdrawn before the check. Weekly path: session 5.

goal: End-of-unit showing 1: the copied sequence aligned and strong, a signaled and spaced partner change, and the group recall with no cue (look-fors), plus the recall card (kept).
note: Showing day: set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five dance in the marked zone about 4 minutes each (24) while the rest sit as the audience, cool-down and self-check on the guide 5, room back 3; a group the teacher wants to see again may be recorded on the school device with the family yes (feet, hands or whole body), kept there. A student who cannot move freely dances a seated or one-limb version, mapped to the same look-for. Response to the marks comes on the respond day. Weekly path: session 6.

goal: End-of-unit showing 2: distance, three dimensions, filled and empty space and eyes leading; the improvisation filling the count with and against the accompaniment and in both phrasings; two clear energy qualities.
note: Showing day: set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five dance in the marked zone about 4 minutes each (24) while the rest sit as the audience, cool-down and self-check on the guide 5, room back 3; a group the teacher wants to see again may be recorded on the school device with the family yes (feet, hands or whole body), kept there. Shown to a partner class. Weekly path: session 7.

goal: Second try at the parts marked not yet on either showing, then the portfolio piece (the recall card or a drawing of the group dance) with its reflection line.
codes: DA:Pr5.1.3a; DA:Pr5.1.3b; DA:Pr5.1.3c; DA:Pr4.1.3a; DA:Pr4.1.3b; DA:Pr4.1.3c
note: Respond: groups from the record sheet (at most four) take a second try at the part marked not yet with the teacher; the others rehearse in pairs from the written move; one piece goes into the portfolio folder with a one-line reflection. Weekly path: session 8.

goal: Hook: the class watches Paul Taylor Esplanade, described and linked, sees walking, running and sliding turned into a dance, and meets the compelling question about where ideas come from.
note: Work: Esplanade (1975). Responding and connecting touched. Hazards and controls: floor cleared and checked for spills and objects before the session; bare feet or soft-soled shoes, never socks on a smooth floor; an arm length between dancers when traveling; level changes slow, knees and hands first; no lifts and no weight-sharing; partner contact only by agreement and never required; the stop cue used; water and rest offered. Weekly path: session 9.

goal: Starting points shown in steps: a picture, a poem, a sound, an object or a place becomes a move; each student tries moves from two starting points of their own and keeps both on the starting-point list.
note: Retrieval task (10 minutes after the warm-up): grade 2 idea sources and linked moves, and a dance people and place. By course order: one ten-minute reteach of both grade 2 steps together for a student or class that did not take the grade 2 year. set-up 3, warm-up 5, retrieval 10, teaching 15, cool-down 4, room back 3. Free path: pictures from old magazines, found objects, poems read aloud. Weekly path: session 9.

goal: Starting-point trials: three quick rounds, two trials each, one chosen and danced again.
note: Baseline look at the unit main look-for, rotating groups, marked met, partly or not yet; not scored, it is the first of two marks for growth. Weekly path: session 10.

goal: The challenge card shown: a teacher-set movement challenge (feet never at the same speed twice; three shapes on different body parts), several solutions tried, one chosen and shown with a one-line reason.
note: The movement-challenge model starts here. Challenge cards ask for nothing higher than a small jump on the floor. Weekly path: session 10.

goal: Esplanade watched again for its relationships (friends and a group), compared with a relationship of the student own, an invented child or a story character, in the frame "The dance shows ___. It is like ___."
note: Ties to the student own life are invited, never required; the invented child line is marked the same. Health steps if a student tells something. Weekly path: session 10.

goal: Challenge rounds: three new challenge cards solved in pairs, one solution chosen each time with its reason said aloud.
note: Shorter year: fold-in day (see the scope and sequence). Weekly path: session 11.

goal: The class watches Katherine Dunham L'Ag'Ya, described and linked, and links its moves to the Martinique fighting dance she studied, saying what they reveal about the people who danced it.
note: Sensitivity: Dunham also studied ceremonies in Haiti; the unit uses L'Ag'Ya only, a stage work, and no ceremony; the fighting dance is watched, and students moves never strike or touch. Two-ties card. Weekly path: session 11.

goal: The class watches a Dancing Earth piece about caring for water or seeds, described and linked, and each group writes a research question about the view the dance takes.
note: Sensitivity: the agent reads the company published words and a Native-run source first; dancers named by their own nations as the company names them; watched only, no imitation, no regalia, no ceremony. The issue stays a school-safe question; no student takes a side in a public dispute. Weekly path: session 12.

goal: Research in groups: the answer found on two short Curio Class research cards and the key idea explored in movement; each group sets its showing with some choice: a challenge solution, moves from a chosen starting point and the research moves.
note: Research cards written from the company own pages and a public agency page on the issue (Candidate kept: two short cards a grade 3 student can answer from). Creating and connecting. Weekly path: session 12.

goal: Critique day: each group shows for a partner group, takes describe, ask and suggest comments and chooses one change.
note: The unit one critique (describe, ask, suggest), each comment tied to a look-for, praise alone is not feedback; the teacher marks the record sheet; each group chooses one change and says it in one line. Weekly path: session 12.

goal: The change rehearsed; each student finishes the starting-point card and the reason line on the challenge card, and each group the research card line on what the moves helped them notice.
note: Step cards withdrawn before the check. Weekly path: session 13.

goal: Run-through of the showing with the self-check on the guide, two rounds, a partner group watching.
note: Weekly path: session 13.

goal: The like-me and two-ties frames said aloud on the studied dances in pairs (practice, not scored).
note: The frames were met on days 5 and 7 of the unit. Weekly path: session 13.

goal: End-of-unit showing: moves from the chosen starting point with both trials on the kept card, a new challenge card solved with its reason, and the research moves with the research card (look-fors and kept cards).
note: Showing day: set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five dance in the marked zone about 4 minutes each (24) while the rest sit as the audience, cool-down and self-check on the guide 5, room back 3; a group the teacher wants to see again may be recorded on the school device with the family yes (feet, hands or whole body), kept there. Weekly path: session 14.

goal: End-of-unit written day: the relationship in an unseen described dance compared with one of the student own or the invented child, and two moves of an unseen described dance linked to the culture on its work card with what they show.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the unseen Curio Class phrase danced or the unseen description read twice (4), written items at seats, read aloud, at most three a student, one to three sentences, a drawn or spoken answer marked the same (15), show items at the teacher spot by group of five, about 2 minutes each (12), others finish a kept card, room back 3. The invented-child option is marked the same. Response comes on the respond day. Weekly path: session 15.

goal: Second try at the parts marked not yet, then the portfolio piece (the starting-point or research card) with its reflection line.
note: Respond: groups from the record sheet (at most four) take a second try at the part marked not yet with the teacher; the others rehearse in pairs from the written move; one piece goes into the portfolio folder with a one-line reflection. Weekly path: session 16.

goal: Year 3 mid-year check: a showing in groups of five sampling unit 1 only: a copied sequence recalled with the body aligned and no cue, then danced again after one coach comment and the student's own check on the alignment card; an improvisation that fills a new set count with two energy qualities, staying with the music's timing and phrasing on the beat. Unit 2 end-of-unit records (days 30 and 31) are carried unscored; no unit 2 id is scored again.
note: Course-level check, no written part: set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five at about 4 minutes each (24), cool-down 4, cool-down and room back 4: 40 minutes; at most two look-fors a student in a group turn; no item scored twice. Two look-fors a student: the recalled aligned sequence, improved after one coach comment and the student's own check (DA:Pr5.1.3a with DA:Pr5.1.3c, each part), and the improvisation with two qualities kept on the music's timing and the beat phrasing (DA:Pr4.1.3b with DA:Pr4.1.3c, each part). A new count and a new sequence, not the unit 1 task. Task form (lead call 6): a showing is the discipline's own evidence and may follow the unit showing; the items here are new (a new count, sequence and coach step on earlier-unit work), so no item repeats inside two weeks. Weekly path: session 17.

goal: Respond to the check: second tries at the parts marked not yet, then the year dance rehearsed toward the next unit.
note: Course-level respond: the teacher returns the check marks; groups with a not yet take a second try with the teacher, the others rehearse the year dance in pairs; asks no test of any child. Weekly path: session 18.

goal: Hook: the class watches Trisha Brown Accumulation, described and linked, and meets the compelling question about pattern and form.
note: Work: Accumulation (1971). Hazards and controls: floor cleared and checked for spills and objects before the session; bare feet or soft-soled shoes, never socks on a smooth floor; an arm length between dancers when traveling; level changes slow, knees and hands first; no lifts and no weight-sharing; partner contact only by agreement and never required; the stop cue used; water and rest offered. Weekly path: session 19.

goal: The tools card shown in steps: repeat a move, reverse it, add one move at a time; the class makes a simple pattern with each tool.
note: Retrieval task (10 minutes after the warm-up): grade 2 central idea in the middle of a dance, and clues to meaning across styles. By course order: one ten-minute reteach of both grade 2 steps together when needed. set-up 3, warm-up 5, retrieval 10, teaching 15, cool-down 4, room back 3. The choreographic-tools model starts here. Weekly path: session 19.

goal: Accumulation watched again: the class spots how one move added at a time builds the whole phrase and names the pattern in move order.
note: Words: pattern, phrase. Weekly path: session 19.

goal: Tools drill: one short phrase repeated, reversed and accumulated, three rounds with the step card.
note: Baseline look at the unit main look-for, rotating groups, marked met, partly or not yet; not scored, it is the first of two marks for growth. Weekly path: session 20.

goal: AB and ABA forms shown with the start-middle-finish card; pairs build a short AB and then an ABA from their tool patterns.
note: Words: AB, ABA. Form card. Weekly path: session 20.

goal: The class watches a non-devotional kathak solo and an Irish step dance piece, both described and linked, and fills the two-traditions chart: the arms, the upper body, the rhythm of the feet, what is alike and what differs.
note: Sensitivity: kathak temple and court history in one plain sentence from the named dancer or a cultural body page; no bells or costume; no hand gesture of devotional meaning copied (leave-out line). Irish step dance: no hard shoes. Class talk practices ELA SL.3.1, taught in ELA grade 3 unit 1 (weeks 1 to 8); the critique card shows the talk rules. Weekly path: session 20.

goal: The class phrase danced two ways from step cards written from named practitioners published teaching (telling arms and spins; still arms and quick feet), with one difference told each time.
note: Spins slow, three at most in a row, stop on the cue (dizziness); stamping soft in bare feet. Weekly path: session 20.

goal: Two-ways drill: the class phrase switched between the two traditions on the drum signal, three rounds, a partner naming the difference.
note: Shorter year: fold-in day (see the scope and sequence). Weekly path: session 21.

goal: A phrase that shows a feeling or idea built in steps; the class picks movement clues in a teacher phrase and says how they tie to its main idea.
note: Words: style. The dance-look-describe-interpret routine. Weekly path: session 21.

goal: Groups build an ABA dance with a named tool, its A section a phrase that shows a feeling or idea of their choice.
note: Creating. This ABA dance is the one revised and staged in unit 4. Weekly path: session 21.

goal: Critique day: each group dances its ABA for a partner group, takes describe, ask and suggest comments and chooses one change.
note: The unit one critique (describe, ask, suggest), each comment tied to a look-for, praise alone is not feedback; the teacher marks the record sheet; each group chooses one change and says it in one line. Class talk practices SL.3.1. Weekly path: session 22.

goal: The change rehearsed; each student writes the kept line on how one choice helped show the feeling or idea and names the tool on the form card.
note: Step cards withdrawn before the check. Weekly path: session 22.

goal: Run-through with the self-check, then the response frames said aloud on the studied works (pattern in move order, a clue and its idea, alike and different).
note: Practice, not scored. Weekly path: session 22.

goal: End-of-unit showing: an AB or ABA form danced with a tool named on the kept form card, and the phrase showing its feeling or idea with the kept line.
note: Showing day: set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five dance in the marked zone about 4 minutes each (24) while the rest sit as the audience, cool-down and self-check on the guide 5, room back 3; a group the teacher wants to see again may be recorded on the school device with the family yes (feet, hands or whole body), kept there. Shown to a partner class. Weekly path: session 23.

goal: End-of-unit written day: the pattern that builds the unseen teacher phrase, a clue and its main idea, one way two traditions on new work cards are alike and one way they differ; then the class phrase shown both ways at the teacher spot with one difference told.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the unseen Curio Class phrase danced or the unseen description read twice (4), written items at seats, read aloud, at most three a student, one to three sentences, a drawn or spoken answer marked the same (15), show items at the teacher spot by group of five, about 2 minutes each (12), others finish a kept card, room back 3. Candidate kept: each written item read aloud a second time for a student who reads below grade 3, inside the slack. Weekly path: session 24.

goal: Second try at the parts marked not yet, then the portfolio piece (the form card or a drawing of the ABA) with its reflection line.
codes: DA:Cr2.1.3a; DA:Cr2.1.3b; DA:Re7.1.3a; DA:Re7.1.3b; DA:Re8.1.3a; DA:Re9.1.3a
note: Respond: groups from the record sheet (at most four) take a second try at the part marked not yet with the teacher; the others rehearse in pairs from the written move; one piece goes into the portfolio folder with a one-line reflection. Weekly path: session 25.

goal: Year 3 year-end check: written part first on two new described dances (two moves linked to the culture on the work card; a relationship compared with one of the student own or the invented child), then the showing (a partner level, direction and path change; moves from a starting point the student picks from three new starting-point cards). Unit 3 records (days 48 and 49) carried unscored; unit 4 is assessed by its family showing.
note: Course-level check: set-up 3, warm-up 2, written part first with every student seated, the unseen piece danced or read twice (10), then six groups of five at about 3 minutes each (18), cool-down and room back 5: 38 minutes; at most two look-fors a student in a group turn; no item scored twice. Draws on units 1 and 2 only, so it does not repeat the unit 3 assessment just given. The invented-child option is marked the same. Task form (lead call 6): a showing is the discipline's own evidence and may follow the unit showing; the items here are new (new described dances and starting-point cards on earlier-unit work), so no item repeats inside two weeks. Weekly path: session 26.

goal: Respond to the check: second tries at the parts marked not yet, then the year dance rehearsed toward the next unit.
note: Course-level respond: the teacher returns the check marks; groups with a not yet take a second try with the teacher, the others rehearse the year dance in pairs; asks no test of any child. Weekly path: session 27.

goal: Hook: the class watches Oskar Schlemmer Triadic Ballet, described and linked, sees costumes built as shapes change how a body moves, and meets the compelling question; the unit 3 ABA dance is danced through.
note: Work: Triadic Ballet (1922). Fallback: a class that left out unit 3 learns a short Curio Class original study on days 1 to 3. Hazards and controls: floor cleared and checked for spills and objects before the session; bare feet or soft-soled shoes, never socks on a smooth floor; an arm length between dancers when traveling; level changes slow, knees and hands first; no lifts and no weight-sharing; partner contact only by agreement and never required; the stop cue used; water and rest offered. goal: The stage map shown: stage left, stage right, center, upstage, downstage marked in tape, named from the dancer view and used to place each dancer.
note: Retrieval task (10 minutes after the warm-up): grade 2 chosen change and level symbols, and separate zones and a staging extra. By course order: one ten-minute reteach of both grade 2 steps together when needed. set-up 3, warm-up 5, retrieval 10, teaching 15, cool-down 4, room back 3. The stage-terms model starts here. Weekly path: session 28.

goal: Stage-area calls: the teacher names an area and dancers travel there and freeze, then each student labels a stage sketch with the five areas.
note: Baseline look at the unit main look-for, rotating groups, marked met, partly or not yet; not scored, it is the first of two marks for growth. The labeled sketch is kept. Weekly path: session 28.

goal: Using feedback shown in steps with the feedback card (describe, ask, suggest, then change, then say what changed), modeled by the teacher on a sample phrase.
note: The feedback-loop model, met in unit 1, is owned here. Weekly path: session 28.

goal: The floor map shown: arrows and symbols for travel directions and paths, read and drawn for a short teacher phrase.
note: Maps use arrows and symbols only; no grid, scale or measuring (math contact). Weekly path: session 29.

goal: Map-symbol drill: dance a path from a map, then map a path a partner dances.
note: Weekly path: session 29.

goal: The class watches kabuki dance Fuji Musume, described and linked, for its painted scenery, live shamisen music and on-stage costume change, then tries a costume piece, music, scenery or a light in its own dance.
note: Sensitivity: every kabuki role played by men, said plainly if asked; no kimono, wig or face paint, no imitation of Japanese people; the agent reads a Japanese cultural body page first. Costume pieces paper or card over clothes, never over the face or eyes. Light: flashlights only, never at eyes, no flashing. Free path: paper costume pieces, a painted paper backdrop, a song sung by the class. Weekly path: session 29.

goal: Groups try two design choices in the set space and keep one, and draw the floor map of their ABA dance.
note: Creating and performing. Weekly path: session 29.

goal: Critique day: partner groups give describe, ask and suggest feedback on the ABA dance; each student fills the change card (the suggestion, the change, one line describing it).
note: The unit one critique (describe, ask, suggest), each comment tied to a look-for, praise alone is not feedback; the teacher marks the record sheet; each group chooses one change and says it in one line. Weekly path: session 30.

goal: The change rehearsed on the marked stage, each dancer starting and finishing in a named area; the program card names the design choice.
note: Candidate kept: the program card written by the students, one line each (10 minutes), read aloud at the showing. Family yes asked in the family note for the showing outside class; no photographs without it. Weekly path: session 30.

goal: End-of-unit family showing on the marked stage: the change seen, each dancer in the named area, the kept design choice used and named on the program card; the change card, floor map and stage sketch scored after the session.
note: Showing day: set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five dance in the marked zone about 4 minutes each (24) while the rest sit as the audience, cool-down and self-check on the guide 5, room back 3; a group the teacher wants to see again may be recorded on the school device with the family yes (feet, hands or whole body), kept there. The family showing in weeks 27 to 32 is the unit own assessment. Weekly path: session 31.

goal: Second try at the parts marked not yet (a map redrawn, an area entrance fixed), then the portfolio piece with a one-line reflection on the year.
note: Respond: groups from the record sheet (at most four) take a second try at the part marked not yet with the teacher; the others rehearse in pairs from the written move; one piece goes into the portfolio folder with a one-line reflection. Weekly path: session 32.

goal: Hook: the class watches bomba, a named living group, described and linked, sees a dancer sharp moves call the lead drum and the drummer answer, and meets the compelling question.
note: Sensitivity: bomba roots among enslaved Africans on Puerto Rico sugar plantations said in one plain sentence from a Puerto Rican cultural body or museum page, read first by the agent; no skirt work or costume. Hazards and controls: floor cleared and checked for spills and objects before the session; bare feet or soft-soled shoes, never socks on a smooth floor; an arm length between dancers when traveling; level changes slow, knees and hands first; no lifts and no weight-sharing; partner contact only by agreement and never required; the stop cue used; water and rest offered. Weekly path: session 1.

goal: Balance shown in steps on top of the alignment check: a held balance placed inside a copied pattern, then recalled.
note: Retrieval task (10 minutes after the warm-up): unit 1 aligned sequence and recall, and space, time and energy. For a student new to the band or meeting this year first, the ten minutes are the reteach of the earlier step. set-up 3, warm-up 5, retrieval 10, teaching 15, cool-down 4, room back 3. Weekly path: session 1.

goal: Balance recall: the copied pattern with its balance danced three times with a partner coach.
note: Baseline look at the unit main look-for, rotating groups, marked met, partly or not yet; not scored, it is the first of two marks for growth. Weekly path: session 2.

goal: The strengthening routine shown in steps (wall push, knee plank, calf rises, a slow reach, a longer travel) for strength, range of movement and staying power.
note: No plank held more than 20 seconds; water and rest offered. Weekly path: session 2.

goal: The invented dancer card read aloud: how her warm-up, technique and food choices connect to avoiding injury; pairs explain the links in the frame "This helps because ___."
note: Sensitivity: no task asks about a student own diet, weight or body; food choices studied through the invented dancer only. Candidate kept: the card read by the health course lens for its food line before use (a unit plan step, no day). Weekly path: session 2.

goal: Fixed and changing shapes that fill space and leave it empty, small jumps landed softly, and eye contact with a partner; the class watches legong for its held balances and quick eye focus.
note: Sensitivity: Bali also has sacred dances never danced for show; legong is made for watching, studied by watching, no costume or headdress, eye moves tried only as focus (leave-out line). Small jumps on each student own spot, landing softly through the feet and knees; on an unsuitable floor jumps are low and without impact. Weekly path: session 3.

goal: The rhythm card shown: steady and uneven patterns in claps; pairs play a simple part on two safe sounds for a partner to dance to, and dancers react when the tempo changes.
note: Equipment: a hand drum or a pot and wooden spoon, a box drum, shakers or claps; moderate volume. Counts clapped, never written. Weekly path: session 3.

goal: Drum-and-dance rounds: partners swap drummer and dancer through steady, uneven and changing tempos.
note: Shorter year: fold-in day (see the scope and sequence). Weekly path: session 4.

goal: Cues shown: a music cue, a held card and a cue the dancers give one another; groups match phrases on each, then use feedback to set the group next goal and one goal of each student own on the goal card.
note: Paper path: a sheet of card raised as the cue meets the lighting part of the id in full. Weekly path: session 4.

goal: The energy word bank shown: the class analyzes the energy changes in a teacher phrase, names them in vivid words, then refines the phrase.
note: The energy-words model starts here. Weekly path: session 4.

goal: Drum-and-dance groups build their showing with some choice: shapes, a balance, a tempo change and a dancer cue.
note: Creating touched by the drum-and-dance pairs. Weekly path: session 5.

goal: Critique day: each group shows for a partner group, takes describe, ask and suggest comments and sets its goal and each student goal on the goal card.
note: The unit one critique (describe, ask, suggest), each comment tied to a look-for, praise alone is not feedback; the teacher marks the record sheet; each group chooses one change and says it in one line. Weekly path: session 5.

goal: The change rehearsed toward the goals; groups run cue starts and tempo changes until they move together.
note: Step cards withdrawn before the check. Weekly path: session 5.

goal: End-of-unit showing: a balance in the recalled pattern; the group starts together on a dancer's cue and changes on the drum or the held card, with its goal card; fixed and changing shapes with soft landings and eye contact; each student plays the part on two sounds once, dances a steady and an uneven pattern, and dances once through a tempo change.

goal: End-of-unit written day: from a new invented dancer card, how warm-up, technique and food choices connect to avoiding injury; the energy changes of the unseen phrase in two vivid words and one refinement; two moves of the routine shown with alignment at the teacher spot.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the unseen Curio Class phrase danced or the unseen description read twice (4), written items at seats, read aloud, at most three a student, one to three sentences, a drawn or spoken answer marked the same (15), show items at the teacher spot by group of five, about 2 minutes each (12), others finish a kept card, room back 3.
